small_guidance:
- Enable TF32 in `tl.dot` (`allow_tf32=True`) — currently set to False which is forcing slower FP32 mma. For M=N=K=8192 this alone should yield a large speedup on Ada/Ampere.
- Add wider tile autotune configs (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 with num_warps=8, num_stages=4) and drop the small-K configs (BLOCK_K=32) since K=8192 is large; prune unused configs to cut autotune overhead.
- Since M, N, K are all multiples of the largest tile, skip the K-tail mask inside the inner loop (use unconditional `tl.load`) — removes per-iteration mask compute on the hot path.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite to multiply weight directly without the transpose: load B with strides `(stride_bn, stride_bk) = (K, 1)` from `self.gemm.weight` (shape [N, K]) so the K-axis is contiguous on both A and B loads; this removes the one-time `.t().contiguous()` and matches the natural Linear layout.
- Consider a split-K or persistent-kernel design for the 1024x8192x8192 GEMM: with only 64 (M-tiles) × 64 (N-tiles) = 4096 programs at 128×128 tiles, occupancy is fine, but a persistent kernel with L2-aware swizzle (GROUP_M=8) and stream-K can better balance the 128 SMs of the 4090.
- Use FP16/BF16 accumulation path: cast x and weight to BF16 once (cached), accumulate in FP32 with `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` or BF16 inputs — this halves memory traffic on the K-loop loads which is the bottleneck at K=8192.
